title: Chip Shop Curry Sauce
subtitle: The British takeaway curry sauce for pouring over chips
excerpt: A mild, slightly sweet curry sauce thickened with onion and a touch of apple, seasoned with curry powder and turmeric. The specific British chip-shop sauce, designed to pour over chips from the fryer.
sourceNotes: Chip shop curry sauce is a British invention of the 1970s, developed by fish-and-chip shops as a simple condiment sauce using mild curry powder. It has no equivalent in South Asian cooking. Recipe developed from first principles, based on the standard chip-shop version common across northern England and Scotland.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring frequently.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch easily and freeze the extra.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days. Reheat gently and thin with a little water if needed.

content.text: Chip shop curry sauce is a mild, slightly sweet, pourable sauce built from softened onion, curry powder, turmeric, and a touch of apple for sweetness, then blended smooth and thinned to a saucing consistency. It is not Indian curry sauce. It is a British invention specific to the chip-shop tradition and designed to be poured over fried chips.
Heat {{sunflower-oil}} of oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add {{onion}} finely diced onions and {{garlic}} crushed garlic cloves. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes until soft and lightly coloured.
Add {{curry-powder}} of curry powder and {{turmeric-ground}} of turmeric. Stir for 1 minute until the spices are fragrant.
Add {{plain-flour}} of flour and stir to coat the onions. Cook for 1 minute more.
Add {{cooking-apple}} of chopped apple and {{stock-chicken}} of stock a little at a time, stirring after each addition to prevent lumps. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Cook for 15 minutes until the onion and apple are completely tender. Blend until smooth with a hand blender or in a jug blender. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Thin with a little more stock if needed to reach a pourable consistency.

rows.cause: Reduced too much or too much flour
rows.fix: Stir in a little extra stock or water to thin. The sauce should pour easily.

rows.cause: Curry powder not cooked long enough
rows.fix: Cook the spices in the oil for a full minute before adding any liquid. This removes the raw edge.

rows.cause: Not enough curry powder or under-seasoned
rows.fix: Taste after blending. Add more curry powder (cook a small amount separately in a spoon of oil for 30 seconds, then add to the sauce) and more salt.

rows.cause: Onions not soft enough before blending
rows.fix: Cook the onions longer before adding the spices. They need to be completely soft to blend smooth.

content.text: Chip shop curry sauce is a British invention with no direct equivalent in South Asian cooking. It emerged in fish-and-chip shops across northern England and Scotland in the 1970s, probably as an alternative to gravy for customers who wanted something sauce-based with their chips. It is particularly associated with Scotland, where chips with curry sauce is a standard takeaway combination, and with northern England. The sauce is mild, slightly sweet from the apple, and not particularly spicy. It is not meant to be Indian food.
